Plan a complete causal story from the request and immutable seed. Return one compact-story-plan.v2 JSON object matching output_schema, with no Markdown or outside prose. Be concise. Never regenerate the seed, a fixture, state hashes, route metadata, coverage triples or projected spatial states.

Choose meaningful character decisions and consequences. Physical truth is not automatically character knowledge; show discovery through established observations/resources. Preserve abilities, world rules, resources and deadlines. Do not demand perfect repair/success unless the request does. The ending must earn the requested resolution rather than declaring it.

Each event's first predicate is its principal actor/action/target. Additional predicates specify actual observation/acknowledgement/details. required_observer requires OBSERVE or ACKNOWLEDGE by that observer. Evidence provenance is derived from evidence_mode; invented rules/clues/lore are forbidden. resulting_state contains only explicit consequences, with complete replacement values at absolute JSON pointers into existing characters' condition/inventory/knowledge/relationships, existing objects' state, or world fields excluding rules/spatial. No revision, route metadata, entity locations, threads, obligations, spatial state, new entities, overlapping paths or conflicting intermediate values within one scene.

Each scene has narrative_purpose, objective and turn. goal_bindings maps each of those fields to a list of EVENT IDs (not predicate refs). Selecting an event means its complete predicate specification supports that goal. Every required event must be selected by at least one goal. ordered_dependencies contains before/after event anchors: event_id and optional predicate_id; omit predicate_id to order the principal actions, or specify it when a particular sub-action must precede another. Code expands complete goal references, so ordered sub-actions remain covered.

Declare physical actions in spatial_operations: id, literal kind LOCATE/MOVE/BLOCK/RELEASE/ACCESS/JOINT_MOVE, subject (the tracked entity or declared carry group), target (destination/constraint target), event_id, and applicable existing edge_id/constraint_id. Do NOT output predicate_id in spatial_operations. Code binds an exact existing predicate or derives a typed physical predicate from that declaration. Example: an event about one character carrying an object may declare MOVE of that object to a destination, plus separate explicit character moves as needed; code does not infer other entities' movement. A narrative verb like MOVES_TO need not be renamed; the typed MOVE declaration supplies the machine predicate. No new passages/entities/locations. JOINT_MOVE requires an explicitly declared group and an established shared hold from a previous scene. Spatial events must permit direct evidence.

Resolve each existing open thread/obligation explicitly with kind, id and an evidence predicate reference in the resolving scene. Code preserves obligation details and sets SATISFIED only for declared resolutions; references do not prove narrative entailment. All initial entries must be resolved by the last scene. Optional existing-state preconditions are verified against projection, not patched.

Use exactly the requested number of scenes, unique safe scene IDs, and requirement-to-predicate bindings for every request requirement. Optional defaults may be omitted. Code derives frozen inputs, route progression, spatial state/locations, allowed paths and goal source text/triples, while existing structural/semantic guards still check the expanded proposal. Rewrite findings refer to that expanded design; fix their semantic source in this compact proposal. No unresolved questions.

Scene/route IDs must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}; never use paths or spaces.
Return exactly one valid JSON object. Do not include Markdown fences or prose outside the JSON object.
